guideTitle: 6 Best Handheld Showers With Slide Bars in 2026
metaTitle: Best Handheld Showers With Slide Bars 2026
metaDescription: Six handheld shower sets with slide bars compared by bar length, load rating, hose length and install style, to set the head at your height.
mainKeyword: handheld shower head with slide bar
introParagraphs: A slide bar solves the oldest problem with a handheld: where the head hangs. Instead of a fixed bracket at one height, the head rides a vertical rail you can slide up for a tall user, down for someone seated or a child and leave anywhere in between. A good set pairs the bar with a hose long enough to reach, and a few of them double as a grab bar if the listing says so.

The six sets here include the Delta 9-spray slide bar with a stated 500 lb force rating, the BRIGHT SHOWERS 23.6-inch stainless bar rated to 250 lb, the Moen with a 30-inch bar and 69-inch hose, the OFFO with a segmental 24-inch bar, the LOCALAND with a 24-inch bar and a 79-inch hose and the egretshower combo with a drill-free 25.75-inch bar and a rain head.

We evaluated each on bar length, stated load capacity, how it mounts, hose length and spray options. A slide bar is first a mount, and only some are built to take a hand's weight, so we read each listing for what it actually says about support before suggesting it as a handhold.

products.name: Delta 9-Spray Slide Bar Hand Held Shower, Brushed Nickel
specs: Supports up to 500 lb of force
products.description:
Delta's slide bar set is the one here that talks about structure first. The listing says it supports up to 500 pounds of force, that the non-rotating bars increase stability and that the design meets Americans with Disabilities Act standards, and it advises that mounting on wood blocking behind all wall surfaces is preferable. Nine spray settings and a brushed nickel finish round out the handheld.

A non-rotating bar matters because a rotating tube can turn in your hand if you lean on it. The blocking advice is honest: a bar rated to 500 lb only delivers that strength when its fasteners bite into solid framing, so plan the wall behind it before you drill. Read the 500 lb as a statement about the bar and the proper installation.

Compared with the BRIGHT SHOWERS bar it carries a higher stated force rating, and compared with the Moen it focuses on structure over a specific slide length in the text we have. It suits a household that wants a slide bar that can double as a handhold and is prepared to mount it into blocking. If the blocking is not in place, a carpenter can add it from behind a bathroom wall during a renovation, which is the cleanest way to make the rating meaningful.
products.bestFor: A slide bar you may also lean on, mounted into solid blocking.
pros: Listed to support up to 500 lb of force
Meets ADA standards, per the listing
cons: Needs solid blocking behind the wall for the rating
Slide length and hose length are not stated in the text we have
Premium tier relative to simpler sets

products.badge: Best Slide Bar Plus Grab Bar
products.name: BRIGHT SHOWERS Slide Bar Shower Set With Grab Bar, 23.6 Inch
products.description:
BRIGHT SHOWERS pitches this set as a grab bar and a slide bar in one: a 23.6-inch stainless steel bar with a smooth, easy-glide slider and a handheld head. The listing says it supports up to 250 lb and meets ADA shower head specifications. That dual role is the draw for anyone who wants one fixture to do two jobs on the same wall.

Combining a grab bar with a slide bar saves wall space, and a stated 250 lb rating gives you a number to plan around. The tradeoff is that the slider and the head attach to the bar, which can interfere with where your hand wants to grip, so check the layout before mounting. As with any wall bar, the studs behind it set the real strength.

Compared with the Delta it lists a lower force figure but a clearer bar length, and compared with the OFFO and LOCALAND sets it states a support rating, which they do not in the text we have. It suits a bathroom where one fixture has to be both a mount and a handhold. The grab bar role also means the bar is likely to be gripped while wet, so a quick check of the slider lock before each shower is sensible.

ADA shower head specifications, per the listing

products.name: Moen Eco-Performance 5-Function Handheld With 30 Inch Slide Bar
products.description:
Moen's set has the longest slide bar in this guide at 30 inches, plus a 69-inch hose and a 4-3/8-inch handheld with five functions: downpour, rinse, massage, relaxing massage and full spray. It is an Eco-Performance model, which indicates a water-saving design, and the finish is brushed nickel. The listing says it installs onto the existing shower wall.

Thirty inches of travel is generous. It covers the range from a seated child's height to a tall adult's shoulder, so a household with a wide spread of users gets the most out of it. The 69-inch hose is long enough to reach most places without being unwieldy. The listing makes no statement about weight capacity in the text we have, so treat the bar as a mount and not a handhold.

Compared with the OFFO and LOCALAND sets it is a longer, branded bar with a mid-length hose, and compared with the Delta it makes no support claim. It suits a shared bathroom where height range matters most.
products.bestFor: Households with users of very different heights.
pros: 30 in slide bar gives the widest range
cons: No support rating in the text we have
Treat as a mount, not a grab bar
Brand tier is higher than budget sets

products.name: LOCALAND Hand Shower With 24 Inch Slide Bar, 79 Inch Hose
products.description:
LOCALAND pairs a 24-inch slide bar with a 79-inch hose, the longest hose in this guide, and ten spray settings including a turbo wash fan spray the listing says cuts through grime. The internal design is described as high pressure, and the nozzles are rub-clean and anti-clog. The long hose and adjustable height give the most reach and positioning options of the sets here.

A 79-inch hose on a slide bar means you can park the head high, carry it to the tub and still have slack for a seated user. The turbo wash mode turns the head into a cleaning tool, which is useful when the shower doubles as a rinsing station. Ten settings are more than most people need.

Compared with the Moen it has a shorter bar and a longer hose, and compared with the OFFO it has more settings and a stated hose length. The listing gives no support rating in the text we have. It suits someone who wants maximum reach and cleaning ability from a slide bar set. If you rent, keep the original arm and fittings so you can restore the wall when you leave.
products.bestFor: Maximum reach and a cleaning mode on a slide bar.
pros: 79 in hose is the longest here
24 in slide bar adjusts the head height
Ten settings including a turbo wash
cons: No support rating in the text we have
Ten settings are many to learn

products.name: OFFO Shower Slide Bar Combo, 24 Inch Segmental Bar, 6 Modes
products.description:
OFFO builds its 24-inch slide bar from two short rods that you assemble first, a design the listing says makes it easy to line up with the original installation holes. The holder rotates 360 degrees to aim the head, and the 5-inch handheld offers six modes including an oxygenated spray, rain, rain plus massage and massage. The hose is 60 inches.

The segmental bar is a clever answer to a common retrofit problem: old shower arms and wall holes are rarely in the position the new bar wants. Being able to align with existing holes can mean no new drilling in tile. A 60-inch hose is the shortest in this guide, which limits reach for seated use.

Compared with the LOCALAND it has a shorter hose and fewer settings, and compared with the Moen it has a shorter bar. The listing makes no support claim in the text we have. It suits a retrofit where lining up with existing holes saves the tile. Running both outlets together halves what each gets, so use the handheld alone when you want a strong rinse.
products.bestFor: A retrofit where the bar must line up with existing holes.
pros: Two-rod bar aligns with original holes
Six modes including an oxygenated spray
cons: 60 in hose is the shortest here
No support rating in the text we have

products.name: egretshower Rain and Handheld Combo With 25.75 Inch Slide Bar
products.description:
egretshower's combo adds a rain head to the slide-bar idea. It pairs a 4.7-inch handheld with ten settings and a 5.5-inch rain head through a 3-way diverter, on a 25.75-inch stainless steel slide bar that is described as drill-free. The listing counts 82 modes across the combination and says an upgraded pressure design uses air and internal channels to keep each outlet even. A jet cleaning mode is included.

A drill-free bar is attractive for renters and for tile you would like to leave intact, but the listing does not tell us how it attaches in the text we have, so check the mounting method. A combo gives overhead coverage plus a detachable wand on one rail, though splitting the flow softens each outlet. The 82-mode count is a marketing figure for combinations.

Compared with the single-handheld sets it adds a rain head, and compared with the Delta it makes no support claim. It suits a household that wants rainfall, a handheld and an adjustable height without drilling.
products.bestFor: Rain plus handheld on one adjustable bar without drilling.
cons: Mounting method is not described in the text we have

buyingCriteria.explanation: A slide bar is a mount first. The Delta lists 500 lb of force and the BRIGHT SHOWERS lists 250 lb, but the Moen, LOCALAND, OFFO and egretshower sets make no support claim in the text we have. Do not lean on a bar with no rating. If you want a bar that doubles as a grab bar, choose one that says so and mount it into studs or blocking.

The Moen has 30 inches of travel, the egretshower 25.75 inches, the LOCALAND and OFFO 24 inches and the BRIGHT SHOWERS 23.6 inches. More travel lets you set the head lower for a seated user or higher for a tall one. Measure the heights you need before you choose. A bar that is too short limits the benefit.

Hoses run from 60 inches on the OFFO and 69 on the Moen to 79 on the LOCALAND. A slide bar often places the head higher on the wall, so a longer hose gives more reach to your feet or the tub. Several listings omit length. Check before buying.

A set that aligns with your existing holes can save drilling tile. The OFFO two-rod bar is designed for that, and the egretshower is described as drill-free. The Delta recommends blocking behind the wall. Think about your wall before you choose the style.

A slider that glides smoothly and locks firmly makes height changes easy, and a slider that sticks gets ignored. The BRIGHT SHOWERS lists an easy-glide slider. Check that the slider and head do not take over the part of the bar where a hand would naturally grip. Run the slider up and down a few times with a wet hand before settling on a height, because a stiff slider is harder to adjust than it looks.

Settings run from five on the Moen to ten on the LOCALAND and egretshower. A cleaning mode, such as the LOCALAND turbo wash or the egretshower jet, adds a second job. More settings add choices and steps. Match the count to your habits. Count the tasks the head will do, such as rinsing, cleaning and bathing a pet, and pick extras only if they match.

howWeEvaluated.title: Support statements
howWeEvaluated.description: We read what each listing says about load: 500 lb of force on the Delta, 250 lb on the BRIGHT SHOWERS and nothing in the text we have for the others. We credited specific numbers and mounting advice. Sets with no claim were treated as mounts only. We looked at whether the listing tells the buyer where the strength comes from, such as blocking or studs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Height range
howWeEvaluated.description: Bar lengths from 23.6 to 30 inches were compared. We considered users of different heights and seated showering. The Moen led on travel. Retrofit-friendly bars were credited because many bathrooms cannot take new holes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Hose and reach
howWeEvaluated.description: Hose lengths of 60, 69 and 79 inches were compared, and we noted listings that omit length. Reach matters when the head sits high on a bar. Longer hoses scored higher for seated use. Where a rating was stated, we asked whether the mounting advice supported it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Installation approach
howWeEvaluated.description: The OFFO segmental bar, the egretshower drill-free claim and the Delta blocking advice were compared. We favored clear mounting guidance. Retrofit friendliness counted. We treated spray features as secondary to the bar, since the bar is the point of this category.

howWeEvaluated.title: Spray and cleaning options
howWeEvaluated.description: Settings and cleaning modes were compared, including the LOCALAND turbo wash and the egretshower jet. We weighed extras against complexity. A slider that is easy to operate with wet hands was counted as part of the evaluation.

faq.q: Can I lean on a slide bar?
faq.a: Only if the listing says it supports weight. The Delta lists 500 lb of force and the BRIGHT SHOWERS lists 250 lb, and both depend on correct mounting. Others are mounts only, so use a separate grab bar for support. Marking the studs with tape before you drill avoids a second set of holes in tile.

faq.q: How long should a slide bar be?
faq.a: Long enough to set the head at the heights you need, from seated to tall standing. The Moen offers 30 inches and others offer 23.6 to 25.75 inches. Measure the lowest and highest positions you want. A short vertical bar can be mounted beside a long one if you want a dedicated handhold in addition to the head rail.

Usually yes, unless the set is described as drill-free like the egretshower. The OFFO is designed to align with existing holes. If you drill, aim for studs or blocking, as the Delta advises. Slide bars that look the same can differ in how far they sit from the wall, which changes how easy it is to grip the head.

faq.q: How long should the hose be?
faq.a: Long enough to reach your feet from the head's highest and lowest positions. Hoses here range from 60 inches on the OFFO to 79 inches on the LOCALAND. A slide bar lifts the head, so more hose helps. If you share the shower with a child, a lower slider height can be set once and left for the whole routine.

faq.q: Is a rotating bar a problem?
faq.a: A bar that rotates can turn in your hand if you lean on it. The Delta uses non-rotating bars for stability. For a bar you might lean on, choose a non-rotating design. Make sure the bracket fits the connection on your hose, because some brands use slightly different adapters.

faq.q: Can I add a slide bar to my current head?
faq.a: Often yes, since slide bars are sold separately, but check the connection and the hose. A set that includes the head is simpler. A therapist can advise on the best height for seated use. When in doubt, a handyperson can install the bar and test the load in a few minutes.
